what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/hold-one-thing-until-done: whether the required-setup cover stands and the one must-do row the hold shows, from the person's own rows, and each change of their hold setting, written only while it is still what was read.

payload.label: See what holds me
payload.job: Tell me whether my setup still has to be finished before anything else opens, and which one thing I must do now
payload.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Everything it works from is in the request and everything it makes is in the answer. From your setup steps (setup_steps: record:setup-steps rows, or the Get started answer you send as setup), your must-do list (must_do: record:waiting-on-you rows, or the whole waiting answer as things) and your hold setting (state), it answers cover { covered, key }: true while any required step is not done (the page draws only setup until then), null when nothing says, and key, the name your gate row gives the cover (required-setup when it gives none, so a missing key never leaves everything open). Beside it, hold: the one row that unblocks the most by your rank rules, every row that may hold in that order, how many times it can still be set aside today, the ways to hand it back and the stakes for turning the hold off. While the cover stands nothing else is held. Also answers what to keep: jobs (ai-job records for the AI-doable work it removed from the hold, each under a stable id so the same trigger is one job), held_fact ({ key, title } or null, the held thing to keep) and device_runs (the declared device tools to start when the held thing changed from kept_held, the one you last kept).

opens_screens.description: Address starts that open one of your screens; a row done in a place outside them holds only with another control

now.description: The time to decide at (ISO); now when left out

payload.label: Change what holds me
payload.job: Set the one thing I must do aside with a reason, hand it back to my AIs, choose what turning the hold off costs me, ask to turn it off, or turn it back on
payload.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Answers your hold setting after a change, by your hold rules: set-aside needs a reason of the rules' length and lasts the rules' minutes, a few times a day; hand-back gives the rest of the thing to your AIs by one of the rules' ways and leaves the hold; choose-stake picks what turning off costs, in force once the stake before it has run its delay; turn-off takes effect only after the stake's delay and comes back by itself; turn-on is at once. state is your hold setting as you last kept it; the answer holds the whole next setting (state) and the AI jobs the change makes (jobs, ai-job records under stable ids with real producer provenance), for you to keep together.

way.description: One of the rules' hand-back ways (hand-back)

values.description: The values the stake's fields ask for (choose-stake)

now.description: The time to change at (ISO); now when left out

payload.label: Answer the page that shows the one thing that holds me
payload.job: Answer the Trillion page routes GET and POST /work/api/needs-you-hold: the one thing held for me now, and setting it aside, handing it back, choosing a stake, asking off or turning it on
payload.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser, stored } and answers the page with { status, body }; it reads and writes no store: stored.records are the person's records it works from, and it answers the rows to keep (keep) and the device runs to start (runs). GET /needs-you-hold answers 200 with the hold over the person's Waiting on you rows (record:waiting-on-you), their hold setting (setting:needs_you_hold) and their hold rules (setting:needs_you_hold_rules): { on, held, ranked, ..., said, words }; a read that fails answers 503 { error, busy: true }. POST /needs-you-hold with { op, key?, title?, reason?, way?, stake?, values? } (op: read, seen, aside, hand_back, stake, off or on) changes the hold setting on condition of what was read (409 when the store refuses the kept setting), keeps each job the change hands to the person's AIs as an ai-job record once, and answers the change with the read after it; seen marks read the notices the held thing's own device runs told, on this page's surface. Every read keeps the held thing as setting:needs_you_held when it changed; a refused change answers 400 { error }. Any other path or method answers 404.

given.description: Consent records by section id for the shared doer gate.

things.description: Full authoritative waiting answer; preserves every source section and finish control.

pages.description: The results of the reader tools a waiting source names, { [tool id]: [result, ...] }, each reader's results in the order it was run.

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here as { records: [{id, type, value}] } of setting (the row setting:needs_you_hold), setting (the row setting:needs_you_held), setting (the row setting:needs_you_hold_rules), record:waiting-on-you, ai-job (ids starting ai-job:hold-), told-the-person, told-the-person (the row told-the-person), told-the-person (ids starting told-the-person:), record:waiting-sources, ai-job, post, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

keep.description: What the run would keep, for the caller to keep where the person keeps it: rows { id, type, value, expected } (value null removes; expected is the record as it was handed in, or null for a new one, so a store refuses a row whose record moved). The run itself writes nothing.

runs.description: Device tool runs the hold starts: { tool_id, input, key }. The caller starts each through its own run path only after every keep row is written, once per key.
